name: Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, histopathological, and imaging findings

criteria.description: Presence of spindle-shaped endothelial cells with kaposiform morphology on biopsy
Ill-defined, violaceous, infiltrative cutaneous or deep soft tissue mass typically in infants or young children
MRI showing infiltrative soft tissue lesion with ill-defined margins and heterogeneous enhancement
Associated consumptive coagulopathy with thrombocytopenia and hypofibrinogenemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon strongly supports diagnosis but is not always present

laboratory: Thrombocytopenia with platelet trapping in lesion
Hypofibrinogenemia and elevated D-dimers indicating consumptive coagulopathy
Anemia secondary to bleeding and consumption
imaging: MRI showing infiltrative soft tissue mass with ill-defined margins and heterogeneous enhancement
Ultrasound demonstrating hypervascular lesion with high flow
other: Histopathology showing spindle-shaped endothelial cells with slit-like vascular channels
Immunohistochemistry positive for vascular markers CD31, CD34, and lymphatic marker D2-40

distinguishingFeatures: Different histopathological features with more prominent spindle cells and slit-like vascular spaces
More superficial lesion with 'cannonball' tufts of capillaries on histology

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging violaceous mass in infant or young child
Development of Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon with severe thrombocytopenia
Signs of consumptive coagulopathy including bleeding and bruising
references: Drolet BA, Trenor CC 3rd, Brandão LR, et al. Consensus-derived practice standards plan for complicated Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma. J Pediatr. 2013;163(1):285-291.
Croteau SE, Liang MG, Kozakewich HP, et al. Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: a report of 33 cases with clinical, imaging, and pathologic features. J Pediatr. 2013;162(1):142-147.
